promptText: Which hotel brands should an owner consider when evaluating branded residences as part of a hotel project in Europe?

payload.rawResponseText:
An owner should build the brand shortlist around the project’s **location, target buyer, pricing, hotel positioning and service-charge capacity**, rather than simply selecting the most prestigious name.

Europe’s branded-residence market remains predominantly luxury and hotel-led. Savills’ data, accurate as of **January 1, 2026**, identifies Mandarin Oriental, Radisson Blu, Four Seasons, Six Senses and Swissôtel as the leading individual hotel brands by completed and pipeline European projects. At parent-company level, Marriott has the largest European portfolio, while Accor has the strongest pipeline. ([pdf.savills.com](https://pdf.savills.com/documents/branded-residences-europe-report-2026.pdf))

## Recommended brand universe

| Project positioning | Brands to consider | Best suited to |
|---|---|---|
| **Trophy urban ultra-luxury** | **Mandarin Oriental, Four Seasons, The Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, Raffles, Rosewood, Waldorf Astoria** | Prime capital-city or gateway locations; limited, high-value residences; buyers able to support substantial service charges |
| **Ultra-luxury resort** | **Aman, One&Only, Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental, Six Senses, Rosewood, The Ritz-Carlton** | Mediterranean, island, golf and Alpine resorts; villas or large-format homes; international second-home buyers |
| **Wellness and sustainability-led** | **Six Senses, Aman, Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental** | Projects where spa, longevity, nature and wellness programming are central rather than secondary amenities |
| **Luxury lifestyle** | **W, EDITION, SLS, SO/, Mondrian** | Design-led urban or resort projects targeting a younger, socially oriented buyer with strong F&B and entertainment components |
| **European luxury/heritage** | **Kempinski, Raffles, Fairmont, Rosewood, Mandarin Oriental** | Historic conversions, grand hotels and destinations where European heritage and local identity are important |
| **Upper-upscale or broader residential price point** | **Radisson Blu, Swissôtel, Mövenpick, Radisson and selected Wyndham brands** | Larger schemes where ultra-luxury operating standards and service charges would be commercially difficult |
| **Soft-brand/local-identity strategy** | **The Luxury Collection, Autograph Collection, MGallery, Emblems Collection** | Distinctive independent hotels where the owner wants distribution and residential support without imposing a rigid global design identity |

### 1. Brands that should normally make the first-round shortlist

**Mandarin Oriental**  
Arguably the clearest benchmark for European luxury branded residences at present. Savills forecasts 18 European schemes by 2032, making it the region’s leading individual hotel-residence brand. It already has residences in London, Barcelona and Vienna, with projects announced or forthcoming in Madrid, Munich, Athens and elsewhere. ([pdf.savills.com](https://pdf.savills.com/documents/branded-residences-europe-report-2026.pdf))

**Four Seasons**  
A strong choice where service, property management and buyer confidence are more important than design-led lifestyle positioning. Four Seasons reports approximately 6,000 units across 54 residential properties, and a large proportion of its hotel-development pipeline includes residences. ([press.fourseasons.com](https://press.fourseasons.com/news-releases/2024/private-residences-growth/?utm_source=openai))

**The Ritz-Carlton and St. Regis**  
These should usually be tested on any conventional luxury mixed-use project. Marriott offers a broad residential ecosystem across Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, W, EDITION, JW Marriott and other luxury brands, giving an owner several positioning options within one platform. Marriott currently leads Europe at parent-group level with 37 branded-residence projects. ([marriott.com](https://www.marriott.com/luxury/about-us?utm_source=openai))

**Six Senses**  
Particularly compelling for Mediterranean, countryside and Alpine projects where wellness, sustainability and experiential programming can materially differentiate the residences. Six Senses is forecast to have 11 European schemes by 2032, joint third with Four Seasons. ([pdf.savills.com](https://pdf.savills.com/documents/branded-residences-europe-report-2026.pdf))

**Raffles and Fairmont**  
Accor should almost always be invited into a European operator process because it can offer multiple residential positions through Accor One Living. Raffles suits trophy, heritage-led luxury; Fairmont generally works for larger urban and resort schemes. Accor reports more than 130 residential projects under development across over 25 hospitality brands. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/news-stories/accor-one-living-interview-jeff-tisdall?utm_source=openai))

**Rosewood**  
A strong candidate for lower-density, design-sensitive developments requiring a pronounced sense of place. Its residence proposition encompasses ownership, serviced apartments and villa products supported by dedicated residential management. ([rosewoodhotels.com](https://www.rosewoodhotels.com/en/residences?utm_source=openai))

**Waldorf Astoria**  
Worth testing against Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis and Raffles for classic luxury. Hilton’s residential platform now extends across nine brands, although Waldorf Astoria and Conrad remain its clearest luxury-residential propositions. ([hilton.com](https://www.hilton.com/en/corporate/residential-development/?utm_source=openai))

### 2. Specialist additions

- **Aman:** Best reserved for genuinely exceptional, low-density sites with privacy, architecture and very high residential values. Aman already operates residential villas at Amanzoe in Greece and is developing additional resort residences, including Bodrum. ([aman.com](https://www.aman.com/residences?utm_source=openai))
- **One&Only:** Appropriate for exclusive beachfront, island and resort developments rather than conventional urban mixed-use.
- **Kempinski:** A credible European luxury alternative, particularly in Central and Eastern Europe, Turkey, Alpine markets and heritage destinations. It is among Europe’s more active residential brands. ([pdf.savills.com](https://pdf.savills.com/documents/branded-residences-europe-report-2026.pdf))
- **Radisson Blu:** Should not be overlooked for larger upper-upscale projects. It is forecast to have 12 European schemes by 2032, second only to Mandarin Oriental in the Savills European ranking. ([pdf.savills.com](https://pdf.savills.com/documents/branded-residences-europe-report-2026.pdf))
- **Swissôtel and Mövenpick:** Potentially suitable where an internationally recognizable upscale product is needed but the market cannot sustain ultra-luxury pricing or operating costs.
- **W, EDITION, SLS, SO/ and Mondrian:** Add these where design, nightlife, restaurants and social spaces will drive residential demand more than traditional formality. Marriott and Accor/Ennismore both have established residential platforms supporting these lifestyle brands. ([marriott.com](https://www.marriott.com/luxury/about-us?utm_source=openai))

## Suggested RFP shortlist

For a typical luxury hotel-and-residences project in Europe, I would initially invite:

1. **Mandarin Oriental**
2. **Four Seasons**
3. **Ritz-Carlton or St. Regis**
4. **Raffles or Fairmont**
5. **Rosewood**
6. **Six Senses**
7. **Waldorf Astoria**
8. **Kempinski or Radisson Blu**

For a trophy resort, add **Aman and One&Only**. For a lifestyle project, replace two or three traditional luxury brands with **W, EDITION, SLS, SO/ or Mondrian**.

## What the owner should compare

The operator selection should be based on a full residential underwriting exercise covering:

- Evidence of achievable **sales premium and absorption**, using local—not global—comparables.
- Brand licensing, sales, technical-services, residence-management and ongoing HOA fees.
- Required residential amenities and incremental development cost.
- Expected annual service charges and whether target buyers will accept them.
- Allocation of shared hotel/residential costs, facilities and staff.
- Rental-pool structure, owner-use restrictions and local short-term-rental rules.
- Brand contribution to brokerage, launch marketing and international buyer generation.
- Residential management experience distinct from ordinary hotel operations.
- Territorial protection and competing projects in the pipeline.
- Long-term brand standards, refurbishment obligations, termination rights and consequences of debranding.

Savills reports an average European branded-residence premium of approximately **38%**, but this should not be inserted into underwriting without project-specific evidence. The same report emphasizes that location remains the fundamental driver, while 86% of completed European hotel-branded schemes are co-located with a hotel—supporting the operational logic of evaluating the hotel and residences together. ([pdf.savills.com](https://pdf.savills.com/documents/branded-residences-europe-report-2026.pdf))
